core_line: Absence is not empty; absence is a governed evidence condition.
purpose: Organizes records where the death is known through missing witness, missing body, missing name, unclaimed status, delayed certificate, official custody, database trace, or family reconstruction rather than a bedside scene.

titles: Absence is not empty: when the record begins with no bedside witness

Found after days: odor, decomposition, closed doors, and the family’s non-viewable body
No one was there: guilt, reconstructed timelines, and the story family has to make from traces
Negative proof: what the archive must not infer from absence, silence, unclaimed status, or missing remains
No next of kin search: phone trees, public administrators, investigators, and people who do not fit the form
Unclaimed body: identified by name, but not claimed or not claimable
Unidentified remains: when the person’s name is not yet attached to the body
Public or county disposition: cremation, burial, cemetery, and the dignity of the unclaimed
Database grief: searching lists of missing, unidentified, or unclaimed people
Case number as temporary name: when the file becomes the handle for the person
Missing and not known dead: ambiguous loss before any body or certificate
Unrecovered body: drowning, fire, collapse, war, disaster, wilderness, and the funeral without remains
Death abroad or far from home: distance, consulate, translation, repatriation, and not being able to get there
Identification work without spectacle: DNA, fingerprints, dental records, family samples, and the non-public boundary
Death notification: the call, the knock, the unknown number, and the first official sentence
Medical examiner or coroner custody: the body as person, evidence, remains, and responsibility
Pending or deferred death certificate: paperwork limbo before final cause or manner
Personal effects: wallet, phone, clothes, jewelry, keys, and the inventory of a life
No viewing or changed viewing: when the body cannot be seen where the family expects
Delayed funeral because the body is held, examined, identified, or not yet released
